# Phase 0 sketch-kernel benchmark

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

> **Historical artifact:** This records pre-hardening design evidence and does not define the current production method. See `docs/SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md` and ADR 0004.

Date: 2026-08-28
Schema: `phase0-v1`

This benchmark was frozen before running the candidate comparison. The executable,
fixture generator, metrics, and stable TSV writer live in `crates/phase0`; the frozen
contract is in `phase0-contract.md`. Raw results are retained in
`phase0-synthetic.tsv` and `phase0-chm13-chr1-hor.tsv`.

## Synthetic corpus

The deterministic corpus contains 262,144-base identity, substitution, indel, offset,
central-inversion, reverse-complement, low-complexity, tandem-repeat, and unrelated
pairs. Each result is a complete 32 by 32 matrix using `k=21` and 1,024 sketch units.
Exact distinct canonical k-mer sets and MashMap-compatible coordinated bottom-s are
constructed independently.

| Kernel | Mean build (ms) | Mean matrix (ms) | Mean absolute ANI error | Worst fixture p95 | Maximum cell error |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| verification-gated b-bit OPH | 17.521 | 0.571 | 0.000861 | 0.014825 | 0.046179 |
| coordinated bottom-s | 187.353 | 4.970 | 0.000712 | 0.012211 | 0.803123 |
| densified b-bit OPH | 29.571 | 0.628 | 0.001072 | 0.021395 | 0.046208 |
| minmer postings | 242.882 | 0.323 | 0.004079 | 0.030723 | 0.264637 |
| SetSketch-like spike | 14.448 | 19.619 | 0.446676 | 0.906251 | 0.934917 |

All known-orientation diagonal cells with informative evidence were classified
correctly by the four main candidates. The SetSketch-like row is a deliberately small
joint-cardinality spike, not the paper's specialized joint MLE, and its failure does
not constitute a general result about SetSketch.

The initial b-bit implementation failed badly on unrelated cells: one chance truncated
collision can become an apparently high ANI after the `1/k` transform. The production
candidate now requires at least one match in the existing 32-bit verification channel
before accepting the collision-corrected b-bit estimate. A pinned regression test
prevents a b-bit-only collision from creating similarity. The table reports the gated
result; the failing result remains documented in development history.

Coordinated bottom-s had the best mean error but one extreme sparse-evidence indel
cell. This is why maximum-cell behavior remains visible rather than being averaged
away. Postings made the matrix traversal fastest but introduced more repeat-rich bias.
Densification did not help at this interval occupancy and modestly worsened the
low-complexity result.

## CHM13 repeat-rich validation

The exact repeat test uses 262,144 bases beginning at zero-based chr1 coordinate
122,000,000 in RefSeq `NC_060925.1`. This lies inside the chr1 higher-order
alpha-satellite annotation in the official T2T-CHM13v2.0 Cen/Sat v2.1 track. The
downloaded annotation SHA-256 was
`2fecb4bddba9c643c259fc8d2136a59ef070a77c2a76c84ee8645c96da562946`.

| Kernel | Build (ms) | Matrix (ms) | Mean absolute ANI error | p95 | Maximum |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| verification-gated b-bit OPH | 17.420 | 0.688 | 0.000857 | 0.002077 | 0.004093 |
| coordinated bottom-s | 127.572 | 8.905 | 0.000941 | 0.002510 | 0.004153 |
| densified b-bit OPH | 28.322 | 0.635 | 0.000865 | 0.002143 | 0.004212 |
| minmer postings | 178.876 | 1.539 | 0.011922 | 0.018885 | 0.023460 |

The complete 248,387,328-base chr1 browser run remains the chromosome-scale runtime
and memory test; its separate provenance record is `2026-08-28-chm13-chr1.md`.

## Interpretation

The gated b-bit OPH candidate currently offers the best combined construction speed,
matrix speed, tail accuracy, and repeat behavior. The undensified form beat the tested
densification scheme. Per the agreed development order, this is an observation rather
than the formal production-backend decision; final selection and parameter tiers are
deferred until after the UI sprint.

Primary algorithm references: the [Minmers paper](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btad512),
[optimal OPH densification](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/shrivastava17a.html),
and [SetSketch](https://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol14/p2244-ertl.pdf). CHM13 annotation
provenance is maintained by the [T2T CHM13 project](https://github.com/marbl/CHM13).
